thesis: Alarm.com (Nasdaq: ALRM), connected property software and hardware platform. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) and EX-99.1 read. Revenue Q3 279.4M +9%, 9M 822.4M +10%; SaaS and license revenue Q3 191.2M +9.0%; adjusted EBITDA Q3 66.2M +19% (non-GAAP, reconciliation not read); GAAP net income 9M 81.9M vs 97.0M (-16%) as G&A rose 13.5M on IP legal costs and acquisitions (BTR, RGS) added expense. TTM revenue 1,084.0M, NI to common 117.0M, OCF 203.5M, capex 13.3M, FCF 190.2M (6.0% yield; 5.0% after SBC 30.2M). Close 64.99 (2026-11-20, two sources agree) x 49.05M basic shares = 3,188M: 27.2x TTM GAAP earnings, about 21.4x guided 2026 non-GAAP EPS 3.02-3.04 (which excludes SBC), 3.6x book. Cash 534.7M vs 500M 2.25% converts due 2029 (net cash about 35M), plus 229.2M equity-method investments. 9M buybacks 58.5M. FY2026 guide raised: SaaS and license 756.1-756.3M, total revenue 1,101-1,111M, adjusted EBITDA 227-229M. Bought CellGate for 61.7M cash on 2026-10-30. Possible mispricing view not established: steady low-double-digit growth, net cash and repurchases at a mid-20s GAAP multiple; the stock is not obviously cheap.
counterthesis: GAAP earnings fell 16% in 9M while revenue rose 10%; legal costs on three IP matters (EcoFactor seeks injunction and enhanced damages, SkyBell trade secrets, Causam indemnity) are open-ended; hardware revenue (about 345-355M guided) carries lower margin and 9M OCF benefits from payables timing; 229M of equity investments and notes receivable are illiquid and 9M cash paid into them 16.4M; the 2029 converts dilute above their conversion price; adjusted EBITDA excludes SBC about 30M a year; 27x GAAP earnings with single digit SaaS growth is not cheap; peers not compared.
invalidation: Drop if SaaS growth falls below high single digits, an IP ruling imposes an injunction or large damages, hardware margins compress, or FCF after SBC falls toward 3% of market value. Study further only with peers, diluted share basis, reconciliation tables and documented quote origins.
